title: How Forge Works
description: Navigate the Forge learning engine: understand interactive workbenches, live sandboxed DOM preview runtimes, automated assertion evaluators, and mastery evidence progression.

objectives.statement: Explain how the Forge environment executes student code in an isolated live preview sandbox.
Interpret automated assertion feedback to debug code and accumulate evidence toward concept mastery.

content.title: Your Engineering Simulator
content.hook: Forge is not a video player with multiple-choice quizzes — it is a browser-in-a-browser engineering workbench designed to build real muscle memory.
content.context: As you type code into the editor, Forge compiles your markup, stylesheets, and scripts into a sandboxed live preview iframe, running assertions against your real DOM nodes to provide instant engineering feedback.
goals: Understand the three panes: Instructions, Code Editor, and Live Preview.
Learn how automated DOM assertions evaluate your code.
Understand how Forge tracks genuine evidence of mastery across concepts.

content.title: The Forge Workbench Architecture
content.description: Three Core Panes: 1. Left (Instruction & Objectives), 2. Center (Code Editor with Syntax Highlighting), 3. Right (Sandboxed DOM Preview + Live Assertions Engine + Evidence Evaluator).

content.prompt: Why does Forge run student code inside an isolated sandbox iframe rather than directly within the parent application window?
content.code:
<!-- Student Code Running Inside Sandboxed Environment -->
<script>
  document.body.style.backgroundColor = 'salmon';
</script>
options: To isolate student scripts and styles so they cannot interfere with or crash the workbench host application.
Because web browsers can only execute JavaScript if it is inside an iframe.
To slow down rendering and simulate a 1995 dial-up modem.
To prevent students from writing CSS stylesheets.

validation.expected: To isolate student scripts and styles so they cannot interfere with or crash the workbench host application.

feedback.correct: Spot on! The sandboxed iframe provides complete process and security isolation, letting you safely run arbitrary code.
feedback.incorrect: Isolation protects the workbench UI and prevents student scripts from bleeding into the host platform.

content.question: When you click 'Check Solution' in an interactive Forge exercise, how does the system evaluate your work?

options.text: It only checks if your raw text matches a single hardcoded string without running it
It executes your code in the sandboxed preview and evaluates real DOM assertions against the resulting elements and styles
It sends a screenshot to a human grader and waits 24 hours
It automatically marks every exercise complete without checking

content.explanation: Forge evaluates the live Document Object Model (DOM) rendered by the browser, testing actual properties, tag names, computed styles, and accessibility attributes.

feedback.correct: Exact! Forge uses live runtime evaluation against the rendered DOM rather than brittle string matching, so valid alternative coding styles succeed.
feedback.incorrect: Forge actually renders your code in an isolated live preview sandbox and tests the live DOM elements.

content.title: Key Takeaways: Navigating Forge
takeaways: Forge provides a realistic browser sandbox for hands-on frontend engineering.
Code is evaluated against real DOM trees, styles, and behaviors.
Every lesson activity generates verifiable evidence toward your mastery profile.
You are now ready to begin Module 1-1: HTML & Document Structure!
